description: Reviewed word-for-word links for places where the app's edition words a verse differently from the reference SYNONYMS. Applied by scripts/build-verse-word-for-word.mjs after the automatic alignment. Each entry links `surface` (found inside `within` when the words recur) to reference glossary entries and/or an editorial `meaning`; an entry with neither removes the automatic link.

entries.note: Reference reads śrīmad-rādhā; the app reads śrī gāndharvā. śrī keeps the reference gloss of śrīmat.
Gāndharvā is a name of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, so the reference gloss of rādhā applies (the app translation says “Śrī Śrī Gandharvā-Govinda”).
The app reads swāmī śrī bhaktivedānta prabhupādāya where the reference reads śrīmate bhaktivedānta-svāmin iti nāmine; the gloss A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami belongs to these words only.
Editorial: dative of prabhupāda, as in the app translation “Bhaktivedānta Swāmī Prabhupāda”; not glossed in the reference.
Same word as namas te in the next reference praṇāma (Śrīla Prabhupāda Praṇati 2).
Same word and gloss as the opening namaḥ of the reference praṇāma.
Reference reads bheda nā dekhibo; the app reads heribo, a Bengali synonym of dekhibo (“I will see”), so the gloss is unchanged.

entries.meaning: between the forests of Gauḍa (Navadvīpa) and Vraja
entries.note: Editorial: the reference reads gauḍa-braja-jane (“the inhabitants of Navadvīpa and Vraja”); the app reads bane, “in the forests”, matching its translation “the forest of Gauḍa and Vraja”.
Editorial: the reference reads śrī-advaita-sītā (Advaita Āchārya and his wife Sītā); the app reads advaita-chandra, translated “the moonlike Śrī Advaita Āchārya”.
Reference reads kori āś (final a dropped); the app's āśa is the same word, and the automatic alignment lost it to the reordered second line.
Reference reads bolena bolo re; the app repeats bolore (= bolo re, “oh sing!”), so the first one takes the same gloss.
